items.title: A proper dominant morphism with finite function field extension is finite over a neighbourhood of a codimension one point
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a proper dominant morphism of integral schemes with finite extension of function fields is finite over a neighbourhood of any codimension one point of the target (statement lines 2523-2536, tag 02RG-adjacent). The proof notes that the statement follows from a general version over varieties, then gives a direct argument: it reduces to finiteness of the fibre over the point by a properness criterion, goes affine and covers the source by finitely many affine opens, and applies the algebraic criterion for finiteness in codimension one. The reduction and the algebraic translation are the substance, so the claim is H2.
